copy.gary: I've been wandering Pinellas County parks and I still find something new on most visits, like the causeway out to the beach at Fred Howard Park or a quiet trail through Brooker Creek Preserve.
copy.description: Check in at every Pinellas County, Florida park you visit, collect stamps and badges, rate your favorites and explore with your Park Pals.

motifs.name: Heritage Village
motifs.blurb: Heritage Village in Largo is a 21-acre living history museum, with historic homes and buildings moved there from around the county.

motifs.name: Florida Botanical Gardens
motifs.blurb: The Florida Botanical Gardens, next door to Heritage Village, are free to wander, with themed gardens, a wedding garden and native plants.

motifs.name: Brooker Creek Preserve
motifs.blurb: Brooker Creek Preserve, in the county’s northeast corner, protects about 8,700 acres of forest and wetlands, the largest natural area in Pinellas.

motifs.name: Fred Howard Park
motifs.blurb: At Fred Howard Park in Tarpon Springs, a causeway about a mile long leads out to a small beach island in the Gulf.

motifs.name: Wall Springs
motifs.blurb: The spring at Wall Springs Park in Palm Harbor was a bathing spot and health resort in the early 1900s. Today you can see it from an overlook.

motifs.name: The Pinellas Trail
motifs.blurb: The Fred Marquis Pinellas Trail runs the length of the county, from St. Petersburg to Tarpon Springs, for walkers, runners and cyclists.

motifs.name: The sponge docks
motifs.blurb: Greek sponge divers made Tarpon Springs famous. The historic sponge docks are still lined with boats, bakeries and shops.
